h1:
Sa Kaeo in 1 Day
Rong Kluea Market–Sdok Kok Thom
intro: Sa Kaeo is an eastern border province most people know for Rong Kluea Market, the biggest secondhand market on the Thai border. But there's another gem few travelers know about: Sdok Kok Thom, a beautifully restored laterite Khmer temple in Khok Sung district. If you only have one day, both sit in the same Aranyaprathet–Khok Sung zone, so you can easily pair them. This plan takes you shopping at the morning market, over to the Khmer temple late morning, then a local lunch in town before heading back, with the things you need to know about the border situation that you should check before you actually set off.

blocks.html: The day's two highlights sit close together in the eastern part of the province. Rong Kluea Market is in Ban Khlong Luek, Aranyaprathet district, right next to the border checkpoint, while Sdok Kok Thom temple is in Khok Sung subdistrict, Khok Sung district. It's about a 40–50 minute drive from the market to the temple, so a single day is plenty if you want to shop for secondhand finds in the morning, walk the Khmer temple late morning, and wrap up with lunch in Aranyaprathet town. The plan below follows real times you can actually keep, and you can speed it up or slow it down as you like.

blocks.title: Check before you set off (important)
blocks.html: Sa Kaeo is a Thai–Cambodian border province. There have been tense periods, and some checkpoints and sites have closed temporarily in the past. Before you go, check the latest situation, checkpoint hours, and what documents you need through the Sa Kaeo provincial page, the Sdok Kok Thom Historical Park page, and official announcements every time. If the checkpoint or temple is closed on your travel day, switch your plan to other spots in the province instead.

blocks.text: The one-day plan at a glance

blocks.html: This plan splits into three parts. In the morning you walk Rong Kluea Market for secondhand finds while it's still cool and the stalls are fully stocked. Late morning you drive to Sdok Kok Thom temple in Khok Sung. In the afternoon you head back into Aranyaprathet town to eat and pick up souvenirs. Total distances are short, which suits anyone with their own car or a rental for the day, since the temple sits outside town and public transport doesn't reach it.

items: Morning — Rong Kluea Market (Border Friendship Market), Aranyaprathet, shop for secondhand goods
Late morning — Sdok Kok Thom temple, Khok Sung, see the laterite Khmer temple
Afternoon — lunch in Aranyaprathet town + grab souvenirs before heading back

blocks.html: Start the day at Rong Kluea Market, officially called the Border Friendship Market, in Ban Khlong Luek, Ban Mai Nong Phai subdistrict, Aranyaprathet, right next to the Khlong Luek–Poipet border crossing. This is the biggest secondhand and wholesale market in Thailand. Stalls sell everything from secondhand clothes, bags, and shoes to odds and ends, kitchenware, and toys. People come to stock up on cheap goods and unusual finds you don't see elsewhere. Go a little early and you'll have an easier walk, fully stocked stalls, and no harsh midday heat yet.

The market had quietened down for a while because of the border situation, but after the Thai–Cambodian ceasefire signed in late 2025, vendors on both the Thai and Cambodian sides have gradually started reopening their stalls and the atmosphere is slowly picking back up. Even so, the number of stalls open on any given day still depends on the situation, so check before you go whether the market is operating normally that day.

items: Secondhand goods — graded secondhand brand clothes, bags, and shoes, prices from tens to hundreds of baht, haggling welcome
Household and odd finds — kitchenware, toys, spare parts, and bits and pieces that are hard to find elsewhere
Snacks — there are food stalls and snack spots scattered through the market, so you can graze while you shop

Clothes, bags, household goods. Walk a few zones and compare prices before buying

items.activity: Break for a snack in the market

blocks.title: Shopping tips
blocks.html: You can haggle at nearly every stall, so walk around and check a few prices before you commit. For secondhand clothes, spread them out and check for flaws before you pay, and carry cash since many stalls still take cash only. As for crossing over to the Poipet side, always check the checkpoint situation and your documents first. Don't plan a border crossing yet if you're not sure the checkpoint is operating normally.

blocks.text: Late morning — Sdok Kok Thom temple

blocks.html: The day's other highlight is Sdok Kok Thom temple, in Ban Nong Ya Kaeo, Khok Sung subdistrict, Khok Sung district, about a 40–50 minute drive from Rong Kluea Market. The temple is built of laterite and sandstone in the Khmer Khleang–Baphuon style, dating to roughly the 10th–11th centuries CE, and it's the largest Khmer temple in eastern Thailand. Its standout features are the lintels and the Sdok Kok Thom inscription, which records the line of Khmer kings and ancient rituals, making it an important piece of historical evidence. The Fine Arts Department restored it using the anastylosis method (dismantling and reassembling the original stones), a process that took years until it stood tall again. Around the temple is a wide historical park, easy to walk and photograph.

Sdok Kok Thom Historical Park is normally open daily from 08:30 to 16:30 and there's no entry fee yet. There's an information center where you can read up on the temple's story before you go in to see the monument itself. It gets especially busy on the days when the sun aligns through the temple's gateway arch, which happens only a few times a year, so if you want to see that you'll need to check the dates with the park in advance.

items: The temple itself — a beautifully restored laterite Khmer temple, walk around to see the lintels and carved patterns
Information center — tells the story of the Sdok Kok Thom inscription and the restoration, stop here first and you'll understand more
Park grounds — a wide, shaded area, good for photos, with quiet corners to sit and rest

blocks.title: What to bring
blocks.html: The temple is out in the open, and by afternoon the sun is strong with little shade, so bring a hat, sunglasses, and your own water. It's a historical monument, so don't climb on or lean against the temple, and because it sits close to the border, check beforehand whether the park is open normally on your travel day, since it has closed temporarily under official orders during tense periods in the past.

blocks.text: Lunch in Aranyaprathet — what to eat

blocks.html: Head back into Aranyaprathet town to eat. The food around here has a strong Vietnamese and Chinese influence — nam neuang, Vietnamese kuai chap, and braised noodles. We've picked spots that locals and passers-through mention often and that are actually open, so you can choose based on how your day is going. Some places shine for their noodles and broth, others for the Vietnamese dishes, so go with whatever you're craving. Prices are rough ranges depending on the dish and how many plates you order.

items.name: Keng Tom Tun Aranyaprathet
items.blurb: A noodle and pork-leg-rice shop locals go to often. Known for its fragrant braised broth, tender meat, and big pieces of pork leg over rice — a filling lunch before you drive on. Open morning to afternoon.

items.name: Yai Tam Vietnamese Food
items.blurb: A Vietnamese spot the neighborhood recommends. Known for nam neuang, fried spring rolls, and Vietnamese kuai chap, all nicely balanced — good for a light bite or for ordering several dishes to share.

items.name: Braised Duck–Soft Pork Noodle Shop
items.blurb: A roadside noodle shop with an air-conditioned section. The standouts are braised duck and big slices of soft pork in a well-balanced broth — good for a comfortable lunch out of the heat.

items.name: Chicken Rice–Crispy Pork Rice in Town
items.blurb: A one-plate rice shop in Aranyaprathet town with chicken rice, pork leg rice, crispy pork rice, and big bowls of pork blood soup. Quick, filling, and good value — many of these places take cash only.

items.name: Stir-Fry Shop in Town
items.blurb: If your group all wants something different, a made-to-order stir-fry shop in town has all the familiar dishes — krapao, pad see ew, tom yum — easy to order and fast. Good before you travel on.

items.name: Cafe in Aranyaprathet Town
items.blurb: Aranyaprathet has several new cafes with a nice atmosphere, serving coffee, matcha, cake, and bingsu — good for a cool drink and a rest after a full day of market and temple.

blocks.title: Match the real pace
blocks.html: Many of the noodle and pork-leg-rice shops in Aranyaprathet open from morning to afternoon and sell out fast. If you've got your eye on one, don't roll in much past 3 pm. Many small shops take cash only, so keep cash on hand, and checking a shop's page beforehand on a weekday is a safer bet.

blocks.text: Grabbing souvenirs before you head back

blocks.html: Before heading back you can pick up souvenirs two ways. The first is to go back to Rong Kluea Market and stock up on more secondhand goods or wholesale-priced household items. The other is to buy local food in Aranyaprathet town, like nam neuang, moo yor, and fermented goods, which Vietnamese restaurants often sell to take home too. These are the souvenirs people love carrying back from Sa Kaeo — pick ones that keep a bit longer if you have a long drive.

items.name: Rong Kluea secondhand goods
items.blurb: Head back to stock up on cheap finds at Rong Kluea Market — clothes, bags, and household goods at wholesale prices.

items.name: Nam neuang–moo yor
items.blurb: The Vietnamese-style foods Aranyaprathet is known for. Vietnamese restaurants often have take-home sets.

items.name: Fermented and dried goods
items.blurb: Foods that keep well, sold at markets in town. Good to carry back if you've got a long drive.

blocks.text: Getting there and making the day trip work

blocks.html: Sa Kaeo has no airport, so most people come by their own car from Bangkok via Highway 33 (Suwannason), about 3–4 hours to Aranyaprathet, or take a bus/van on the Bangkok–Aranyaprathet route, and there's also a Bangkok–Aranyaprathet train. If you come by public transport, you'll want to arrange a rental car or motorbike for getting around the province, since Sdok Kok Thom temple sits outside town and public buses don't reach it. The whole plan doesn't involve much driving, but the sights sit right along the border, so always check the situation first.

items: From Bangkok — drive Highway 33 about 3–4 hours to Aranyaprathet, or take a bus/train into town
Within the province — rely on your own car/rental, the temple is outside town and public transport doesn't reach it
Border matters — check the situation, checkpoint hours, and documents before every trip. If the checkpoint or temple is closed, adjust your plan

faq.q: What can you do in Sa Kaeo in one day?
faq.a: A single day fits the Aranyaprathet–Khok Sung zone nicely. Start by walking Rong Kluea Market for secondhand finds in the morning, drive to Sdok Kok Thom temple in Khok Sung late morning, then head back into Aranyaprathet town for lunch — braised noodles or Vietnamese food — and finish by grabbing souvenirs before you head back.

faq.q: Where is Rong Kluea Market, and is it operating normally now?
faq.a: Rong Kluea Market (the Border Friendship Market) is in Ban Khlong Luek, Aranyaprathet, next to the border crossing, and it's the biggest secondhand market in Thailand. After the Thai–Cambodian ceasefire signed in late 2025, vendors have gradually started reopening their stalls, but the number open each day still depends on the situation, so check with the provincial page before you go.

faq.q: What time does Sdok Kok Thom temple open, and is there an entry fee?
faq.a: Sdok Kok Thom Historical Park is normally open daily from 08:30 to 16:30, with no entry fee yet, in Khok Sung subdistrict, Khok Sung district. Because it sits close to the border, it has closed temporarily under official orders during tense periods, so before you go, check with the park's page or the Fine Arts Department that it's open normally that day.

faq.q: Do you need to be careful about the border when visiting Sa Kaeo?
faq.a: Yes, be careful and prepared. Sa Kaeo is a Thai–Cambodian border province, and there have been tense periods with some checkpoints closing at times. Before you go, check the latest situation, checkpoint hours, and required documents through official announcements. If you're not sure, don't plan a border crossing yet, and have backup spots ready in case somewhere is closed.

faq.q: Can you visit Sa Kaeo in a day without your own car?
faq.a: Walking Rong Kluea Market in Aranyaprathet town works fine by public transport, but Sdok Kok Thom temple sits outside town and public buses don't reach it. If you want to hit both in one day, we'd suggest renting a car or motorbike, or hiring a local driver to take you there and back.
